name: SWE-Gym
size: 2,438 train instances from 11 Python repos (HF split count)
summary: Real GitHub issue tasks with FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS tests, built for training and verifying SWE agents. Lite (230) and Raw (64,689 unvalidated PR rows) variants exist.
caveats: Small. Only 2.4k tasks, so pass-rate filtering leaves little. Repo overlap with SWE-bench test repos is a known contamination concern for SWE-bench evals. Images must be built or pulled separately.

name: SWE-smith
summary: Synthetic bug-injection tasks generated per repo (LM-written, rewritten, procedural and PR-mirror bugs) with test-based validation and per-task Docker image names. Java and other-language variants are listed under SWE-bench on HF.
caveats: Synthetic bugs are easier and less natural than real issues; problem statements are LM generated. Nemotron-Cascade used it as one of five sources, not alone. Check test-leak risk: FAIL_TO_PASS tests are present in the repo image.

name: SWE-rebench (nebius, v1)
summary: Continuously mined Python GitHub issue tasks with install configs, F2P/P2P tests and docker_image names, from Nebius; also feeds a decontaminated leaderboard.
caveats: The huge test split is unfiltered: some tasks have ambiguous statements or weak tests. Underlying repo licenses vary (license_name column). Check time overlap with your eval set.

name: SWE-rebench V2
summary: Language-agnostic executable SWE tasks with pre-built images, F2P/P2P tests and LLM quality filtering. A companion set has 126,300 PR-derived tasks.
caveats: PR-derived tasks lack issue text quality guarantees. Images are large. Repo licenses vary (license column). Leaderboard maintained for V1 Python only per HF discussion.

name: R2E-Gym (Subset)
summary: Procedurally generated executable environments from commits (back-translated issue text, LM-generated tests) used to train SWE agents and verifiers; includes dev splits in the Lite variant.
caveats: Problem statements are back-translated, tests partly LM-written, so label noise exists. Code repo last pushed 2025-07-13. The Lite variant card has no license field.

name: SWE-bench-extra
summary: Nebius earlier large SWE-bench-format task collection (patch, test_patch, F2P/P2P, license per instance), precursor to SWE-rebench.
caveats: No image columns, so environments must be reconstructed. Superseded by SWE-rebench.

name: SWE-bench (full, train/test splits)
license: MIT (GitHub repo; HF card has no license field)
size: 2,294 test + 225 dev instances in the HF repo; no train split listed
summary: The original 2,294-issue benchmark, now with eval_script, image and log_parser columns. A SWE-bench-Train subset (1,063 questions per the Nemotron-Cascade card) was used by Nemotron-Cascade.
caveats: The HF repo currently exposes test/dev only (verified 2026-11-24). Train data cited by Nemotron-Cascade came from princeton-nlp/SWE-bench; repo overlap contaminates Verified/Lite evals. Git history leak was patched upstream (PR 471).

name: SWE-bench-Live
size: 1,000 test, 1,888 full, 300 lite, 500 verified instances (split counts)
summary: Continuously updated issue-resolution benchmark with docker_image, test_cmds and rebuild_cmds per task, intended to stay ahead of contamination.
caveats: Designed as eval; training on it burns the contamination guarantee. Split definitions may change between updates.

name: Multi-SWE-RL
size: Community RL dataset, first batch data_20240601_20250331; per-language counts not machine-readable on the card
summary: ByteDance Seed community effort to collect multilingual SWE RL instances (unannotated new instances plus discarded Multi-SWE-bench instances).
caveats: Unannotated and license is vague ('other'). Last HF update 2025-07-23. Little documentation of sizes in the card, so size is not verified.

name: SWE-Dev
summary: Feature-driven development tasks: product requirement, partial source, developer-written unit tests and ground-truth code, supporting SFT and RL with test-based reward.
caveats: Exact train/test counts not verified here. A separate zai-org/SWE-Dev-train holds SFT/RFT trajectories (17,871 sft, 2,276 rft rows) with no license on its card. GitHub code repo has no license.

name: SWE-Synth
license: none stated on dataset card (null in API)
summary: Synthetic bug-fix instances with setup patches, F2P/P2P tests and problem statements, plus Moatless SFT trajectories in sibling datasets.
caveats: No license on card, so redistribution rights unclear. Last updated 2025-03.

name: SWE-Flow / Repo2RLEnv swe_flow recipe
size: SWE-Flow code; Repo2RLEnv sample set FineEnvs/repo2rlenv-swe-flow has 100 Harbor tasks
summary: Test-driven synthesis: trace passing tests, remove exercised functions, ask the agent to reconstruct them, reward via retained tests. Hugging Face Repo2RLEnv now packages the recipe as Harbor tasks.
caveats: Sample HF set is only 100 tasks with mixed source licenses. SWE-Flow repo last pushed 2025-06-29 with 40 stars.

name: Repo2RLEnv
summary: Hugging Face tool that turns any repository into verifiable RL environments for coding agents in Harbor task format (instruction, Dockerfile, tests, reward script).
caveats: Young project; recipe quality varies. Verify tests cannot be edited by the agent in each generated task.

name: OpenSWE (GAIR, daVinci-Env)
license: other (gated, access conditions on card); code repo licensed per GitHub as NOASSERTION; search snippet says AGPL-3.0 (unverified)
size: 10K-100K rows (HF size category); paper claims 45,320 Docker environments
summary: Large open set of executable Python SWE environments with synthesis pipeline released.
caveats: Gated with auto-approval; license ambiguous. Counts from paper abstract via search, not confirmed from API.

name: Lego-RL-2699 and LegoFlow-SWE
size: 1K-10K Harbor RL environments (HF size category); Verified-500 packaged as Harbor tasks
summary: SWE-Lego family: Harbor-format RL environments, teacher trajectories and a Harbor-packaged SWE-bench Verified for evaluating against the same trainer.

name: Nemotron-Cascade-RL-SWE

summary: NVIDIA recipe data for SWE RL: difficulty-filtered mix of SWE-Bench-Train, SWE-rebench, SWE-smith, R2E-Gym-Subset and SWE-Fixer, with repos from SWE-bench Verified excluded to avoid contamination.

name: HumanEval
summary: Function-from-docstring Python problems with unit tests, introduced with Codex. The original functional-correctness benchmark.
caveats: Execution-based (unit tests). Saturated: current frontier models are near ceiling, so differences are mostly noise. Public since 2021 and widely copied, so contamination is likely in web-scale pretraining data; the EvalPlus paper also showed the original tests are too weak (see HumanEval+). Measures short self-contained function synthesis only; not repo context, debugging, or design. Historical score in the paper abstract: Codex 28.8% (arXiv 2107.03374).

name: HumanEval+ (EvalPlus)
size: 164 problems (test split), with many more tests per problem than HumanEval
summary: HumanEval with test suites expanded by LLM- and mutation-based input generation to catch plausible-but-wrong solutions.
caveats: Execution-based. Per the EvalPlus README, HumanEval+ has 80x more tests than HumanEval. Same 164 prompts, so prompt-level contamination and saturation concerns remain; it fixes weak tests, not leakage. Python function level only.

name: MBPP+ (EvalPlus)
summary: MBPP subset, cleaned of broken tasks and given 35x more tests, for stricter checking of basic Python generation.
caveats: Execution-based. The EvalPlus README states v0.2.0 trimmed MBPP+ from 399 to 378 tasks by removing broken ones. Entry-level problems, near saturation for strong models; public data so contamination is possible.

name: MBPP (Mostly Basic Python Problems)
size: 974 tasks total; HF splits: train 374, validation 90, test 500, prompt 10
summary: Crowd-written entry-level Python tasks with three asserts each.
caveats: Execution-based but with only about three asserts per task and known broken or ambiguous items (the reason EvalPlus cleaned it). Saturated and public since 2021, so contamination is likely. Entry-level skills only.

name: MultiPL-E
size: Translations of HumanEval and MBPP to 18 additional languages (about 157-161 problems per HumanEval language config)
summary: A system that transpiles unit-test-based Python benchmarks to many programming languages, with prebuilt translated sets.
caveats: Execution-based. Inherits HumanEval and MBPP's saturation and contamination issues, and translated problems stay simple function-level tasks. Low-resource-language results are sensitive to translation artifacts. Per-config counts seen on the HF card: 157, 161, 161, 158 (first four configs).

name: HumanEval-X
size: count not verified (derived from HumanEval's 164 problems)
summary: Multilingual extension of HumanEval with generation and translation tasks, released with CodeGeeX.
caveats: Execution-based. Same saturation and public-data contamination concerns as HumanEval. Exact language list and problem count not verified in this pass.

name: HumanEvalPack (OctoPack)
size: 164 problems per config (test split), several language and task configs
summary: HumanEval extended to six languages and to fix, explain and synthesize tasks, used to evaluate instruction-tuned code models.
caveats: Execution-based for fix and synthesize variants. Derived from HumanEval so saturation and contamination apply. Task and language list not re-verified here beyond split counts.

name: CRUXEval
size: 800 Python functions (3-13 lines) with input and output prediction tasks
summary: Tests code reasoning and execution understanding: predict the output for a given input, or an input for a given output.
caveats: Not purely 'run the model's code': graded by executing assertions on the model's predicted input or output. The paper found many models with high HumanEval scores did not show the same gains on CRUXEval. Public since January 2024; model-generated functions, so leakage and saturation by reasoning models are plausible.

name: LiveCodeBench Pro
size: Quarterly and biannual splits, e.g. quater_2025_1_3 166, quater_2025_4_6 167, biannual_2025_1_6 333 problems
summary: Olympiad-medalist-annotated problems from Codeforces, ICPC and IOI, updated continually, with line-by-line analysis of failed model submissions.
caveats: Execution-based (judged against tests; companion testcase dataset exists). Per the paper abstract (arXiv 2506.11928), without tools the best model scored 53% pass@1 on medium and 0% on hard problems at the time of writing (June 2025); current numbers will differ. Freshness helps contamination but old splits are public.

name: LiveOIBench
size: 403 problems from 72 contests across 14 Informatics Olympiads (2023-2025), about 60 official tests each
summary: Olympiad-level competitive programming benchmark using official test cases and offline judging, with human-contestant percentile comparison.
caveats: Execution-based. Per a search result summary of the paper, GPT-5 reached about the 82nd percentile versus top human contestants usually above the 90th (not independently verified in this pass). I did not verify a data link or license, so only the paper is linked.

name: CodeElo
size: Codeforces-derived problem set (count not stated in metadata I read)
summary: Competition-level benchmark that submits solutions to Codeforces to obtain human-comparable Elo ratings, avoiding the need for private tests.
caveats: Submission-based (execution on Codeforces judge). Relies on an external platform and its rate limits; the paper motivates it by missing private tests and special judges in LiveCodeBench and USACO. Dataset and repo (QwenLM/CodeElo, no license field) were last updated in early 2025.

name: USACO benchmark
license: no license field in GitHub metadata; HF mirror gated (manual)
size: 307 USA Computing Olympiad problems with unit tests, reference code and analyses
summary: Olympiad programming problems with episodic inference methods (retrieval, self-reflection).
caveats: Execution-based. Public since 2024, so contamination is likely. The paper abstract reports GPT-4 at 8.7% pass@1 zero-shot CoT, which frontier models have since far exceeded. The HF mirror vectorzhou/USACO is gated.

name: BigCodeBench
size: 1,140 tasks per version split (v0.1.0_hf to v0.1.3+); BigCodeBench-Hard subset has 148
summary: Python tasks requiring calls into many libraries with complex instructions,
caveats: Execution-based with test cases. The GitHub repo (bigcode-project/bigcodebench) is archived as of 2026-11-24, so expect no more updates or fixes. Tasks are single-file Python, not repo-level. Public since 2024, so contamination is possible.

name: BigCodeBench-Hard
license: license not stated in card metadata (parent is Apache-2.0)
summary: Harder 148-task subset of BigCodeBench selected for lower solve rates, cheaper to run.
caveats: Same caveats as BigCodeBench (archived repo, public data). A subset selected on past model failures may drift in difficulty as models improve.

name: EvalPerf (Differential Performance Evaluation)
license: not stated in HF metadata (EvalPlus repo is Apache-2.0)
summary: Efficiency-demanding tasks with expensive generated inputs and a compound metric that compares the speed of model solutions to reference solutions.
caveats: Execution-based but measures runtime, so results depend on hardware and load. Covers only Python function tasks drawn from existing benchmarks.

name: ClassEval
summary: Manually crafted class-level generation tasks (multiple interdependent methods), about 500 person-hours to build.
caveats: Execution-based. Tiny (100 tasks), so noisy. The paper found LLMs do much worse on class-level than HumanEval-style method-level tasks.

name: DS-1000
size: 1,000 data science problems across 7 Python libraries
summary: StackOverflow-derived NumPy, Pandas, etc. problems with multi-criteria execution plus surface-form checks, with perturbed problems to reduce memorization.
caveats: Execution-based. Per the paper only 1.8% of accepted Codex-002 solutions were incorrect. Library versions are pinned and old, so modern API behavior can differ; public since 2022.

name: CodeScope
summary: Execution-based multilingual, multitask benchmark covering code understanding and generation across many languages.
caveats: Execution-based (per paper). Noncommercial license restricts use in some pipelines. Low adoption and last updated 2023-12, so no maintenance signal.

name: SWE-bench (full)
license: dataset card license not in HF metadata; harness repo is MIT
size: 2,294 test instances (plus dev 225, train 19,008) from 12 Python repos
summary: Real GitHub issue plus repository; the agent must produce a patch that passes the repo's own tests (FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS).
caveats: Execution-based. Public since 2023, 12 repos only, so contamination and repo overfitting are real concerns. Runs need Docker images and substantial disk.

name: SWE-bench Lite
license: dataset card license not in HF metadata; harness repo MIT
summary: A cheaper filtered subset of SWE-bench for faster iteration.
caveats: Execution-based. Small (300) so noisy; contamination applies as for SWE-bench. Many instances have narrow or flawed tests (see SWE-bench Verified entry).

name: SWE-bench Verified
license: dataset card license not in HF metadata; harness repo MIT
summary: 500-task subset screened by human annotators for solvable, well-specified problems; long the headline agentic coding number.
caveats: Execution-based. OpenAI (post dated 2026-02-23) stopped reporting it: of 138 problems o3 did not consistently solve, 59.4% had material test or description issues (35.5% narrow tests, 18.8% wide tests), and all tested frontier models could reproduce gold patches or verbatim details for some tasks, suggesting training exposure. Epoch AI's review page also rates it as flawed (per a search snippet). Python only, 12 repos.

name: SWE-bench Multimodal
size: test 480, dev 100 (current HF card; earlier princeton-nlp copy listed 510/102)
summary: JavaScript and front-end issue tasks where the problem statement includes images such as screenshots.
caveats: Execution-based. Visual inputs are part of the task. Counts differ between the old and new HF copies, so pin the revision you use.

name: SWE-bench Multilingual
summary: Issue-resolution tasks in C, C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, PHP, Ruby and Rust, runnable in the SWE-bench harness with prebuilt images.
caveats: Execution-based. Public data (PRs from 2017-2025 per card), so older instances may be seen in training. Only 300 tasks, so wide confidence intervals.

name: Multi-SWE-bench
size: 1,632 instances in Java, TypeScript, JavaScript, Go, Rust, C, C++
summary: Multilingual issue-resolving benchmark annotated by 68 experts from 2,456 candidates.
caveats: Execution-based. License is 'other' in HF metadata, so read it. Public data, so contamination is possible.

name: SWE-Bench Pro
license: license not in HF metadata (public set drawn from copyleft repos per paper)
size: 1,865 problems from 41 repos: public 731, held-out 858, commercial 276 (paper). HF test split shows 731 rows.
summary: Long-horizon, enterprise-style tasks with a public set, a private held-out set, and a commercial set from proprietary startup repos, designed to resist contamination.
caveats: Execution-based. Only the public 731 are open, so held-out and commercial scores come from Scale. OpenAI first recommended it (2026-02-23), then retracted that on 2026-07-08, estimating about 30% of tasks broken (200 tasks, 27.4%, flagged by an automated pipeline; 249, 34.1%, by human annotation). Paper v2 abstract says performance stays below 45% pass@1 under a unified scaffold.

name: Terminal-Bench 3.0
summary: Next Terminal-Bench generation, mirrored from the GitHub repo at tag v3.0.0 and runnable through Harbor.
caveats: Execution-based. I could not confirm the release date or differences from 2.x from the card, and saw no scores. Terminal-Bench 1 (harbor-framework/terminal-bench-1) is the older, easier set.

name: Aider Polyglot benchmark
license: no license field in GitHub metadata (aider itself is Apache-2.0)
size: 225 Exercism exercises in C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, Python, Rust
summary: Hard Exercism exercises where the model must edit files in aider's format and pass tests, measuring instruction following plus multilingual editing.
caveats: Execution-based. Aider's leaderboard (updated 2025-11-20 when I read it) lists gpt-5 (high) at 88.0% in a run dated 2025-08-23, indicating near saturation at the top. Exercism exercises are public and widely seen in training. Small tasks, not repo-scale.

name: Spider 2.0
summary: Real enterprise workflows over BigQuery, Snowflake and local databases with 1,000+ columns, requiring metadata search, dialect docs and multi-step SQL.
caveats: Execution-based. Much harder than Spider/BIRD, so not saturated. Some settings require access to commercial cloud warehouses.

name: RepoBench
summary: Repo-level code completion with retrieval (R), completion (C) and pipeline (P) tasks in Python and Java.
caveats: Mostly exact-match and edit-similarity, not execution-based. Built from public GitHub code, so contamination is likely for models trained on it.

name: CrossCodeEval
size: multi-language cross-file completion set (count not extracted)
summary: Completion tasks that cannot be solved without cross-file context, in several languages, with static-analysis-based construction.
caveats: Match-based metrics, not execution-based. Built from open-source repos so leakage possible. Task count and language list not extracted in this pass.

name: SAFIM (Syntax-Aware Fill-in-the-Middle)
summary: FIM benchmark focused on syntactic structures (blocks, conditionals, API calls), with problems sourced after April 2022 to reduce contamination.
caveats: Per the paper, execution-based tests for algorithmic subsets; the contamination window is limited to data after April 2022 so newer models may have seen it.

name: CanItEdit
summary: Hand-crafted instructional code editing problems with descriptive and lazy instruction variants, tested by execution.
caveats: Execution-based. Small (105). Python only; public since 2023-24. GitHub repo license field shows NOASSERTION; HF card says MIT.

name: DevEval (SDLC benchmark, arXiv 2403.08604)
size: multi-stage tasks, four languages (counts not extracted)
summary: Evaluates LLMs across the software lifecycle: design, environment setup, implementation, acceptance and unit testing. Note the name clashes with other 'DevEval'/'DevBench' projects.
caveats: Part LLM-judged, part test-based. I did not find a verified data release in this pass. Title is a case study, not a mature leaderboard.

name: ProjectEval
summary: Project-level generation benchmark with three input levels, evaluated by simulated user interaction plus code similarity.
caveats: Benchmark built by an LLM with human review; uses simulated user interaction for execution. I did not verify a repo or data link.

name: Commit0
summary: Agent must implement a library from its spec using interactive unit tests; measures long-form spec following.
caveats: Execution-based (unit tests). Small (54 libraries). Repo last pushed 2026-02. Libraries are public so leakage is possible. HF dataset metadata has no license field.

name: MLE-bench
summary: Agents train models, prepare data and run experiments on real Kaggle competitions, graded against human leaderboards.
caveats: Execution and leaderboard-based. Paper abstract: o1-preview with AIDE reached at least bronze in 16.9% of competitions (2024). Needs Kaggle data downloads and GPUs.

name: PaperBench
summary: Agents replicate ML papers from scratch; rubric-graded by an LLM judge. Also ported to inspect_evals (paperbench).
caveats: Not execution-only: scoring uses an LLM judge with author-co-developed rubrics. License of the official data not verified here.

name: SWE-Lancer
license: repo openai/SWELancer-Benchmark: no license field; archived
size: 1,400+ freelance Upwork tasks worth $1M in payouts
summary: Independent engineering tasks graded by end-to-end tests plus managerial decisions, mapped to real payouts.
caveats: Execution-based for IC tasks (e2e tests triple-verified), proposal-matching for manager tasks. The original GitHub repo is archived as of 2026-11-24 and only a subset was public.

name: METR time-horizon task suite (HCAST, RE-Bench)
size: tasks from RE-Bench, HCAST and 66 shorter tasks (per paper)
summary: Measures the 50% task-completion time horizon: the human task length models complete at 50% success. Reported to double about every seven months since 2019.
caveats: Per paper abstract, Claude 3.7 Sonnet had about a 50-minute horizon (early 2025). Not all tasks are public (the METR/public-tasks repo is archived). Time horizon depends on human baselines and task mix.

name: CyberSecEval (Purple Llama)
size: multi-suite; insecure code generation plus cyberattack compliance tests
summary: Meta's suite for insecure-code generation and cyber misuse, with later versions adding more tests; also in inspect_evals (cyberseceval_2 to 4).
caveats: Original insecure-code tests use static analysis rules (CWEval's authors criticize unclear specs and impractical evaluation). Not execution-based for functionality. Repo license is mixed, so check it.

name: SecCodePLT
summary: Security benchmark built from validated seeds expanded by mutation, with dynamic tests for both code generation and cyberattack helpfulness.
caveats: Dynamic test-based. Gated (auto-approval). The paper (listed as SeCodePLT on arXiv) claims better coverage than static-rule benchmarks, which I did not independently check.

name: CWEval
summary: Outcome-driven evaluation of both functionality and security of generated code using test oracles for CWE-linked tasks.
caveats: Execution-based. Small, public since January 2025.

name: TestGenEval
size: 1,210 test split (code and test file pairs); 68,647 tests across 11 Python repos (paper)
summary: Unit-test authoring and completion benchmark built from SWE-bench repositories, with a lite subset.
caveats: Execution-based (coverage, mutation). Shares repos with SWE-bench, so overlap with SWE-bench-derived training data is likely. Splits seen: test 1,210, dev 210, train 15,439.

name: SWT-Bench
size: Verified variant 433 instances (HF eth-sri/SWT-bench_Verified_bm25_27k_zsb); also Lite
summary: Agents write reproduction tests for real GitHub issues; a good test fails before and passes after the golden patch.
caveats: Execution-based. Derived from SWE-bench so shares contamination concerns. HF license not stated.

name: Defects4J
size: database of real Java faults (count not extracted)
summary: Classic real-fault Java repair and testing database with infrastructure; used by repair benchmarks such as RepairBench.
caveats: Execution-based. Public since 2014, heavily contaminated in code training data; RepairBench (ASSERT-KTH/repairbench, no license field) is a leaderboard built on it.

name: miniF2F
summary: Formal Olympiad-level problems (AIME, AMC, IMO, coursework) in Lean and other systems for theorem proving.
caveats: Verifier-checked (Lean). Heavily saturated by recent provers and public for years, so contamination is likely. The original openai/miniF2F repo is archived and has fixes elsewhere; use a corrected version.

name: PutnamBench
license: no license field in GitHub metadata
size: 1,692 formalizations of 640 Putnam theorems (Lean 4, Isabelle, partial Coq)
summary: Hard undergraduate competition math formalizations for neural theorem provers.
caveats: Verifier-checked. Maintained with an active leaderboard; repo pushed 2026-11-09. License field absent, so check the repo.

name: EvalPlus CLI
summary: Evaluation framework behind HumanEval+, MBPP+ and EvalPerf with backends for HF, vLLM, Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and Bedrock.
caveats: Python-only function-level benchmarks. Last push 2025-10-02. Sandbox execution runs untrusted code, so use Docker.

name: lm-evaluation-harness (code tasks)
size: General LLM harness; code tasks include humaneval, humaneval_infilling, mbpp, code_x_glue
summary: The standard few-shot LLM harness; code coverage is basic.
caveats: Code tasks are thin; code execution requires explicit opt-in because it runs untrusted code.

name: Inspect AI / inspect_evals
size: Collection of community-maintained evals for Inspect AI
summary: Large eval collection including apps, bigcodebench, class_eval, ds1000, humaneval, mbpp, usaco, swe_bench, swe_lancer, livecodebench_pro, mle_bench, paperbench and cyberseceval_2 to 4.
caveats: Third-party ports can differ in prompts and scoring from the original harness, so scores may not match published numbers. Actively maintained (pushed 2026-11-23).

name: OpenCompass
summary: Includes configs for bigcodebench, cruxeval, ds1000, humaneval (plus, multi, x, pro), livecodebench, livecodebench_pro and mbpp (plus, pro).
caveats: Prompt formats may differ from original releases. Heavy configuration.

name: lighteval
summary: Evaluation library with LiveCodeBench tasks (src/lighteval/tasks/tasks/lcb) among many others.
caveats: Code coverage smaller than dedicated harnesses; I saw LiveCodeBench only.

name: EvalScope
summary: Includes benchmarks for bigcodebench, ds1000, humaneval(plus), live_code_bench, mbpp(plus), swe_bench, swe_bench_pro and terminal_bench.
caveats: Many benchmark adapters; verify scoring against the original before comparing numbers.

name: SWE-bench evaluation harness
summary: Official Docker harness that applies model patches and runs repo tests, used by Verified, Lite, Multilingual and Multimodal.
caveats: Heavy on disk and CPU. Some downstream sets (SWE-bench-Live, Pro) ship their own harnesses.

name: aider benchmark harness
size: benchmark/ directory in the aider repo
summary: Runs the polyglot benchmark in Docker against any model aider supports.
caveats: Last push 2026-05-22. Harness details are in aider docs; not re-verified here.

name: Artificial Analysis (pointer)
summary: Third-party site that aggregates model intelligence and coding indices; useful as a pointer to current coding scores.
caveats: Methodology and the set of benchmarks inside its coding index change; not verified in this pass.

name: Magicoder OSS-Instruct 75K
size: ~75K instruction-response pairs (per dataset name and paper)
summary: Synthetic instructions generated by prompting an LLM with random open-source code snippets (OSS-Instruct) to reduce the bias of purely LLM-invented tasks.
caveats: Card states it was generated by gpt-3.5-turbo-1106 and warns to follow OpenAI's usage policy. No execution verification of solutions. Seeds come from public GitHub code.

name: Magicoder Evol-Instruct 110K
summary: Decontaminated version of theblackcat102/evol-codealpaca-v1 (WizardCoder-style Evol-Instruct on Code Alpaca seeds), decontaminated with the StarCoder/BigCode procedure.
caveats: Parent data was generated with gpt-4-0314 and gpt-4-0613 (per the evol-codealpaca-v1 card), so OpenAI terms apply. Decontamination covers older benchmarks only; recheck against newer evals.

name: Evol-CodeAlpaca v1
size: 100K-1M rows (HF size category); exact count not verified
summary: Open re-creation of the WizardCoder Evol-Instruct code data: Code Alpaca 20K evolved with 10 augmentation strategies and answered by GPT-4.
caveats: Card says gpt-4-0314 and gpt-4-0613 produced the evolutions and answers (OpenAI terms apply). Not decontaminated against modern benchmarks in this original form.

name: Evol-Instruct-Code-80k-v1
summary: Community replication of the WizardCoder Evol-Instruct code data.
caveats: Non-commercial license. Generated with OpenAI models (not verified from the card; the card is minimal).

name: Code Alpaca 20K
summary: Self-Instruct-style code instruction set that started the open code-instruction line; seed of Evol-CodeAlpaca.
caveats: Project README says it was generated with Self-Instruct techniques and notes OpenAI TOS (text-davinci-003 per the Self-Instruct recipe; model name not confirmed on the card). Short, simple tasks; saturated.

name: CodeFeedback-Filtered-Instruction
summary: 287K queries from Magicoder-OSS, Python ShareGPT, Magicoder-Evol and Evol-Instruct, filtered to complexity 4-5 by Qwen-72B-Chat.
caveats: Card warns that part of the data was generated by OpenAI models. Overlaps heavily with Magicoder data. Filter used a model-assigned complexity score, not execution.

name: Code-Feedback (OpenCodeInterpreter)
summary: Multi-turn code data with execution feedback and human-feedback-style follow-ups for iterative refinement (OpenCodeInterpreter).
caveats: Card says part of it was generated by GPT-4-0613 and GPT-3.5-turbo-0613 (OpenAI usage policy applies). The headline 91.6 HumanEval/MBPP average in the paper used synthesized GPT-4 feedback at inference.

name: StarCoder2 self-oss-instruct (SelfCodeAlign data)
summary: Instruction data produced by StarCoder2-15B itself via the SelfCodeAlign pipeline (concept extraction, task generation, sampled responses with tests, execution filter). Used for StarCoder2-15B-Instruct.
caveats: Python only. The paper describes a transparent pipeline without distillation from a stronger model. Quality is bounded by the base model that generated it.

name: CommitPackFT
license: MIT (HF card tag); per-file source licenses are permissive
summary: Filtered subset of CommitPack where commit messages resemble natural-language instructions; basis of OctoPack/OctoCoder instruction tuning.
caveats: Commit messages are noisy even after filtering. Predates modern evals. Contamination with benchmark repos should be checked.

name: CommitPack
license: MIT (HF card tag); per-file source licenses are permissive
summary: Raw commit corpus (code before/after plus message) from which CommitPackFT was filtered.
caveats: Very large and noisy. Not a download for low-resource machines.

name: EditPackFT
summary: Further-filtered CommitPackFT subset formatted for instructional code editing (before code, instruction, after code), used to train CanItEdit-evaluated models.
caveats: Small. Derived from commit messages, so instruction quality varies.

name: OpenCoder opc-sft-stage1
size: 3 configs: filtered_infinity_instruct, largescale_diverse_instruct, realuser_instruct; row counts not read
summary: Stage-1 SFT mix of OpenCoder: filtered general instructions plus large-scale synthetic and real-user code instructions.
caveats: Real-user part is extracted from ShareGPT/WildChat-style conversations, so it inherits their provenance and OpenAI-model responses (card says low-quality responses were regenerated; the generator model was not confirmed).

name: OpenCoder opc-sft-stage2
size: 4 configs: educational_instruct 118,278; evol_instruct 111,183; mceval_instruct 35,943; package_instruct 170,943 (dataset_info, split row counts)
summary: High-quality stage-2 code SFT: educational synthetic, evolved, McEval-style multilingual and package-usage instructions.
caveats: Teacher models per subset not confirmed from the card. Check for overlap with Evol-Instruct and Magicoder.

name: Glaive Code Assistant v3
summary: Synthetic code Q&A from Glaive's data platform; v3 includes v1 and v2.
caveats: Card does not name the generator model, so teacher provenance and terms are unknown. No execution verification stated.

name: Ling-Coder-SFT
summary: Subset of the SFT data used for Ling-Coder-Lite, synthesized with OSS-Instruct and Evol-Instruct style pipelines.
caveats: Card does not name the generator models, so provenance and terms are unclear. Not execution-verified per the card.

name: OpenCodeInstruct (NVIDIA)
size: 5,000,000 instruction-solution rows with unit tests, execution status and LLM judgments
summary: Largest open code instruction set: each row has question, solution, generated unit tests, execution results and an LLM quality assessment, so you can filter by test score.
caveats: Per the paper, solutions, tests and judgments came from Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct (Qwen license terms apply to outputs). Tests are model-written, so a passing row is not guaranteed correct. Python-centric.

name: OpenCodeReasoning-2 (NVIDIA)
size: dataset_info lists 1,398,166 and 1,174,475 rows (two splits; split names and languages not re-checked)
summary: Second release: R1 generations with QwQ critiques and right/wrong judgements, for both code completion and code critique SFT.
caveats: Generations by DeepSeek-R1 and critiques by QwQ-32B (per card fields r1_generation, qwq_critique). Judgement labels are model-produced, not ground truth.

name: Nemotron-Post-Training-Dataset-v1 (code split)
size: code split 1,896,395 rows (dataset_info); also chat 746,622, math 2,044,407, stem 20,662,167, tool_calling 310,051
summary: SFT compilation behind Llama-3.3-Nemotron-Super-49B-v1.5 with reasoning on/off responses; the code split carries reasoning traces.
caveats: Card lists teachers including DeepSeek-R1-0528 and Qwen3-235B-A22B, so those model terms apply. Large; stream it.

name: Llama-Nemotron-Post-Training-Dataset (code)
license: CC-BY-4.0 (card also notes Llama-derived-data redistribution requirements)
size: SFT code split 10,108,883 samples (card table); also math, science, chat and RL configs
summary: Post-training data for Llama-3.3-Nemotron-70B and Llama-3.1-Nemotron-Ultra-253B; v1.1 added 500K code reasoning samples.
caveats: Teachers include DeepSeek-R1, Qwen-2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct, Qwen-2.5-72B, Llama-3.3-70B and Mixtral-8x22B per the card; parts are subject to Llama license redistribution terms. Very large.

name: Nemotron-SFT-Competitive-Programming-v2
size: 336K+ Python and 332K+ C++ samples over 34,799 questions; 40K Exercism-derived; 96.5K text-to-SQL with reasoning (card)
summary: Competitive coding with reasoning and critique, Python Exercism-style exercises (Aider problems decontaminated), and enterprise text-to-SQL records generated with NVIDIA Data Designer.
caveats: Card names DeepSeek-R1-0528 as a generator for the competitive subset; SQL generator not confirmed in the text read. Problem sources have their own licenses.

name: Nemotron-SFT-OpenCode-v1
size: 100K-1M rows (HF size category; exact count not read)
summary: Agentic instruction data for the OpenCode CLI: tool calling, AGENTS.md prompts, agent skills, bash-only tools and clarifying-question tool, in six subsets.
caveats: Per card, questions and skills were synthesized with GPT OSS 120B and solution traces with Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct, so those terms apply. Tied to one harness format.

name: Nemotron-SFT-SWE-v2
license: CC-BY-4.0 plus Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD (API list)
size: ~46K OpenHands agent trajectories plus agentless localization, repair and test-generation subset (card)
summary: SWE-Bench-style data: OpenHands agentic trajectories and agentless sub-task SFT data built from SWE-Bench-Train, SWE-reBench, SWE-Smith and SWE-Fixer-Train.
caveats: Agentic trajectories generated by Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct; agentless responses by DeepSeek-R1-0528 (card). Mostly Python repositories; source issue data has own licenses.

name: Nemotron-Cascade-SFT-SWE
size: size not read (card has per-source question and sample tables)
summary: Agentless-mini style SWE SFT data (localization, repair, test generation) from SWE-Bench-Train, SWE-reBench and SWE-Smith, difficulty-selected and decontaminated against SWE-Bench Verified repos.
caveats: Responses generated with DeepSeek-R1-0528. Excludes repositories present in SWE-Bench Verified, which limits but does not remove all contamination risk elsewhere.

name: Nemotron-Agentic-Tool-Use-v1
summary: Multi-turn tool-use conversations: interactive-agent trajectories (simulated user, agent, tool environment) and general tool-calling, judge-filtered.
caveats: Tool-calling subset uses Qwen3-235B-A22B Thinking and Instruct 2507 per the card; other subset generators not fully read. LLM-judge filtered, tools are simulated.

name: open-r1 CodeForces-CoTs
size: ~10K Codeforces problems with up to 5 R1 traces each; many configs (solutions, solutions_py, decontaminated variants)
summary: DeepSeek-R1 chain-of-thought solutions in C++ and Python for Codeforces problems, used to train OlympicCoder.
caveats: Traces generated by DeepSeek-R1. Problems are from Codeforces. Not all traces are verified correct unless using the verified configs; check the card.

name: open-r1 Mixture-of-Thoughts (code)
license: not stated in API tags (check card)
size: 350K verified R1 traces total; code config 83,070 rows (dataset_info)
summary: Verified DeepSeek-R1 reasoning traces across math, code and science; code part is competitive-programming focused.
caveats: Traces distilled from DeepSeek-R1. License field absent in the API tags, so confirm terms before commercial use.

name: OpenThoughts-114k
summary: DeepSeek-R1 reasoning traces with correctness verification; code rows include test cases and starter code.
caveats: Generated by DeepSeek-R1. Code is a minority of the mix.

summary: Result of 1,000+ controlled data-recipe experiments; each question annotated 16x with QwQ-32B. Trains OpenThinker3-7B.
caveats: Teacher is QwQ-32B (Apache-2.0 model). Not execution-verified per row. Paper reports 51% LiveCodeBench for the 7B model (arxiv abstract).

summary: Teacher-agent traces on nl2bash and InferredBugs (C# and Java bugs) tasks, in the Terminus-2 harness, used for OpenThinker-Agent-v1.

summary: DeepSeek-R1 distillation of the Sky-T1 recipe (code, math, science, puzzles) used for Bespoke-Stratos models; made at about $800 of generation per the card.

name: Sky-T1 data 17K
summary: Training data of Sky-T1-32B-Preview (code and math with QwQ-generated reasoning).
caveats: Card is minimal; teacher model not confirmed here.

name: KodCode-V1-SFT-R1
size: dataset_info lists 268,211 / 210,787 / 4,439 rows across splits (split names not re-checked)
summary: KodCode with DeepSeek-R1 responses kept via test-based rejection sampling; columns include r1_solution, r1_correctness and gpt_difficulty.

name: KodCode-Light-RL-10K
summary: Filtered 10K subset of KodCode-V1-SFT-R1 for RL (GRPO/PPO); card reports GRPO runs on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-1M and Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct.
caveats: Non-commercial. Test cases written by GPT-4o; small and Python-only.

name: Magpie-Qwen2.5-Coder-Pro-300K
summary: Raw conversations built by the Magpie self-synthesis method with Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct; includes task_category, difficulty and quality columns.
caveats: Generated by Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct (card). License tag is 'other'; check Qwen terms. Raw, unfiltered conversations.

name: Tulu 3 SFT Mixture (code parts)

name: The Stack v3 (train)

Opt-out via Am I in The Stack, applied before each patch release. Excludes issues, PRs, Kaggle and docs that came with StarCoder2. v3.1 removed exact duplicates (4.9T to 3.6T tokens), so pin the version. stack-v3-full is an HF bucket, not a dataset, and is huge. summary: Ai2 Rust CLI for exact and MinHash dedup over large JSONL datasets.
caveats: Young project; JSONL input only; less battle-tested.

name: decon (Ai2)
summary: Token-based decontamination tool that finds training documents containing eval instances and writes reports and cleaned datasets.
caveats: Young project; coverage depends on the eval files you supply and on n-gram sampling settings.

name: Dolma toolkit
summary: Ai2 data toolkit: fast Rust tagger/mixer, Bloom filter dedup and mixing used for OLMo corpora.
caveats: Bloom filter dedup is approximate; fits web text better than code.

name: Data-Juicer
summary: One-stop data processing system with 100+ operators for text, code and multimodal data, including code filters and dedup.
caveats: Large surface area; verify operator quality on your code data.

name: DCLM (DataComp-LM)
summary: Framework and baselines for data curation experiments including fastText quality classifier filtering of web text.
caveats: Targeted at web text, not code repos.

name: ScanCode Toolkit
license: NOASSERTION in GitHub API (mixed code and data licenses; verify in repo before redistribution)
summary: License, copyright and package detection engine used by The Stack v2 and v3 for file-level license labels.

name: go-license-detector
license: NOASSERTION in GitHub API (verify in repo)
summary: Go library and CLI to detect open-source licenses in a repository's files, used in earlier The Stack pipelines.

caveats: Repo-level only; Ruby dependency.

name: Qwen3.8-27B

summary: Newest open Qwen generation (Aug 2026): dense vision-language model with thinking mode and gains in coding and long-horizon agentic tasks. A strong post-trained starting point for SFT/RL on a single node, and a mid-size teacher.
caveats: Post-trained checkpoint only: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-Base returned 401 on the HF API so no open base was confirmed. Not a coder-specialized model. Vision encoder adds size. No coding score copied here: the card compares against proprietary models under its own harness settings.

name: Qwen3-Coder-Next (and -Base)
size: 79.7B params total, 3B active (MoE, hybrid Gated DeltaNet + attention), 262,144 ctx
summary: Open-weight coding-agent model from Jan 2026 built for local agents (80B total, 3B active). A Base variant is published for further post-training.
caveats: Instruct supports non-thinking mode only (no <think> blocks). MoE with hybrid linear attention needs recent vLLM/SGLang/Transformers. Base card says trained on 370+ languages; we did not verify vendor benchmark numbers.

name: Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct
size: 480B params total, 35B active (MoE), 262,144 ctx native, 1M with YaRN
summary: July 2025 flagship Qwen coder: large MoE for agentic coding and repository-scale context. Commonly used as a permissively licensed teacher for trajectory distillation.
caveats: Very large to serve. Superseded in the Qwen line by Qwen3-Coder-Next and Qwen3.8. Check output quality per task before trusting distilled data.

name: Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct
summary: Small MoE Qwen3 coder that is easy to fine-tune and serve; the most downloaded recent Qwen coder in HF search (about 1.95M downloads on the check date).

name: Qwen2.5-Coder family (32B shown)

summary: Sep-Nov 2024 code-specialized Qwen family with base and instruct variants from 0.5B to 32B. Still the most widely used open base for code SFT/RL recipes (SWE-smith, OpenHands LM, Open-R1 style work).
caveats: Old by Nov 2026: newer Qwen3.x models beat it. License verified only for the 32B/7B pages fetched; sizes 0.5B-3B may carry different licenses, check before use. Qwen2.5 bases may be contaminated with reasoning-like data (see Dr. GRPO paper).

name: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash

summary: Sep 2026 DeepSeek open MoE with 1M context, MIT licensed; the card describes an encoder-decoder (CED) design with KV-cache compression.
caveats: Needs multi-node serving. Safetensors total (763B) and the card's 552B figure differ (likely vision and other components); we report both. No coding score copied from the card.

name: DeepSeek-V3.2

caveats: Superseded by V4.x. Large MoE.

name: DeepSeek-Coder-V2 (Instruct 236B / Lite)
license: DeepSeek model license (HF 'other: deepseek-license'; code under MIT)
summary: June 2024 MoE code model continued-pretrained from DeepSeek-V2; strong at release, now legacy.
caveats: Legacy. Custom license with use restrictions, not OSI open. Superseded by Qwen3-Coder and DeepSeek V4.

name: Kimi K3.1 Pro
license: Custom 'Kimi K3.1 Pro' license: permissive with conditions (MaaS operators above USD 20M revenue need a separate agreement; attribution above 100M MAU or USD 20M monthly revenue)
summary: Nov 2026 open-weight agentic model post-trained from Kimi K3 with large-scale joint RL; the largest open model checked here.

name: GLM-5.3
license: Custom 'glm-5.3' license: MIT-like with Model-as-a-Service revenue condition (security review above USD 10B revenue)
summary: Aug 2026 Z.ai open model; card says it uses the GLM-5.2 base with gains from post-training only, and claims open-source SOTA on Terminal Bench 3.0.
caveats: Card tables are vendor-run and include proprietary baselines; not independently verified. Large MoE.

name: GLM-5.3-Flash
summary: Aug 2026 smaller GLM-5.3 with new base model, hybrid sparse/linear attention and native multimodality; MIT licensed.
caveats: Still needs a multi-GPU node. Vendor-reported benchmarks only.

name: StarCoder2-15B
summary: Open pretrained code model trained on The Stack v2 with opt-outs excluded; the data and training are documented.
caveats: 2024 vintage, far behind current models. OpenRAIL-M carries behavioral use restrictions. Can emit verbatim training code (card warning).

name: OpenCoder-8B (Base/Instruct)
license: 'inf' license (HF other); card says commercial use supported
summary: Fully transparent code LLM: weights plus data pipeline, ablations and training protocol released. Best choice for studying code pretraining and annealing recipes end to end.
caveats: 8K context is short for agentic work. Custom license, read it. 2024 vintage.

name: Seed-Coder-8B (Base/Instruct/Reasoning)
summary: ByteDance Seed (2025) family built from model-curated pretraining data; base, instruct and RL-trained reasoning variants in one permissive license.
caveats: Data pipeline relies on LLM filtering; training data itself is not released. Mid-2025 vintage.

name: Granite Code 8B Base
summary: IBM enterprise-oriented code model trained on license-permissive data; legacy but cleanly licensed.
caveats: 4K context, April 2024, outclassed. Newer IBM Granite 4.0 models are general-purpose (granite-4.0-h-small, 32.2B, Apache-2.0, verified in API) and not code-specialized.

name: Codestral-22B-v0.1
summary: Mistral's 2024 code model; weights open for research and testing only.
caveats: MNPL forbids production/commercial use; prefer Devstral Small (Apache) or Qwen coders.

name: Devstral Small 2 (24B)
summary: Dec 2025 Mistral agentic coding model, Apache licensed; earlier Devstral-Small-2505 and 2507 are also Apache-2.0 (verified).
caveats: Instruct-only; no base released in what we checked. Card says it performs 'remarkably' on SWE-bench but we copied no number.

name: Devstral 2 (123B)
license: Modified MIT License (see LICENSE file; third-party-rights restriction in card)
summary: Larger Dec 2025 Devstral for agentic coding under a modified MIT license.
caveats: Modified MIT: the exact modification was not fully read beyond the card line. Dense 123B is expensive to serve.

name: Code Llama 70B (legacy)
summary: Meta's 2024 code Llama; included for historical comparison only.
caveats: Legacy, license has usage conditions, far behind current open models.

name: Kimi-Dev-72B
summary: Qwen2.5-72B-based SWE model trained with Agentless-style RL; card reports 60.4% on SWE-bench Verified (Moonshot-reported, workflow approach).

name: SWE-agent-LM-32B
summary: SWE-smith showcase: Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct fine-tuned on 5k SWE-agent trajectories generated with Claude 3.7 Sonnet.

name: DeepSWE-Preview
summary: RL-only coding agent trained on Qwen3-32B with 4.5K R2E-Gym problems (sympy-like repos shared with SWE-bench Verified filtered out); card reports SWE-bench Verified rising from 23% to 42% in 200 RL steps.
caveats: Numbers are from the model card (agentica-org). Config context is 40,960 although agent runs use longer contexts via scaffolding. Preview release.

name: OpenHands LM 32B v0.1
size: 32B params (Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct base); API total not fetched
summary: Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct tuned on SWE-Gym-derived data for the OpenHands agent; card reports 37.2% SWE-bench Verified resolve rate.

name: DeepCoder-14B-Preview
summary: RL fine-tune of DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B for code reasoning; card reports 60.6% Pass@1 on LiveCodeBench v5 (8/1/24-2/1/25), versus 53.0 for the base distill.

name: OpenCodeReasoning-Nemotron-32B
summary: NVIDIA reasoning code model distilled via SFT only from the OpenCodeReasoning dataset on Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct.

name: Nemotron-Cascade-14B-Thinking
size: 14.77B params, ctx 32,768 (YaRN to 90K used for SWE Verified Agentless)
summary: Dec 2025 NVIDIA reasoning model trained with cascaded domain-wise RL (including SWE).

size: 560.5B params in safetensors; card: 550B total, 55B active; 262,144 ctx
summary: Jun 2026 hybrid Mamba-2 plus MoE general model whose card includes SWE-bench Verified and LiveCodeBench rows; a permissively licensed (OpenMDW) very large teacher.

name: Olmo 3 32B (Base/Think)
summary: Fully open (weights, data, checkpoints incl. stage1/2/3) Allen AI model suite with Base, Instruct and Think; best for transparent post-training research. No dedicated 'OLMo-Coder' was found.

name: SmolLM3-3B
summary: Fully open 3B model with dual-mode reasoning; handy as a tiny testbed for code recipes (see smollm repo).

name: gpt-oss-120b
summary: Aug 2025 OpenAI open-weight reasoning model with an Apache license; a permissive teacher/baseline.

name: Skywork-OR1-32B (and 7B)
license: Apache-2.0 per GitHub repo (HF card license field not set)

name: AceReason-Nemotron-14B
summary: RL-only (math then code) from DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B; card reports LiveCodeBench avg@8.

name: Magicoder: OSS-Instruct
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses

name: WizardCoder: Evol-Instruct for code
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: Adapts Evol-Instruct to progressively harder code instructions and fine-tunes StarCoder.

name: OctoPack: Instruction Tuning Code LLMs
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: CommitPack: 4 TB of Git commits across 350 languages used as natural code-instruction data; 46.2% HumanEval pass@1 for StarCoder-16B tuned without OpenAI outputs (abstract).

name: StarCoder 2 and The Stack v2
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: Documents the open data, opt-out and training for StarCoder2 on The Stack v2.

name: OpenCoder: The Open Cookbook
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses

name: Qwen2.5-Coder Technical Report
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses

name: DeepSeek-Coder
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: Repo-level pretraining data construction (dependency-ordered files) and fill-in-the-middle for code models.

name: DeepSeek-Coder-V2
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: Continued pretraining of a MoE on code and math tokens to reach closed-model-level code results at release.

name: CodeRL
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses

name: RLTF: Reinforcement Learning from Unit Test Feedback
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: Online RL with multi-granularity unit-test feedback (including error locations) to refine code LLMs.

name: PPOCoder
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: Combines pretrained code LMs with PPO using compiler/execution and structure-alignment feedback.

name: DeepSeek-R1
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: Shows reasoning can be incentivized with pure RL on verifiable rewards, including coding competitions.
caveats: Full data and code not released; replicate via open-r1.

name: AceReason-Nemotron
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: Systematic RL ablations: math-only RL first then code-only RL; shows math RL also helps code.
caveats: Competitive coding only.

name: Skywork Open Reasoner 1
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: Open RL implementation on R1-distill models; abstract reports average accuracy on AIME24, AIME25 and LiveCodeBench rising from 57.8% to 72.8% for 32B; includes ablations on core RL components.
caveats: Competitive programming only.

name: SWE-Gym
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: First environment for training SWE agents: 2,438 real Python tasks with executable runtimes; up to 19% absolute gains on SWE-bench Verified/Lite via SFT, plus trained verifiers (abstract).
caveats: Only 2,438 tasks from a small set of repos, Python only.

name: SWE-smith
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: Pipeline that turns any Python repo into an execution environment and synthesizes 100s-1000s of task instances by breaking tests; builds a 50k-instance dataset from 128 repos (abstract).
caveats: Synthetic bugs differ from real issues; Python only; trajectories used Claude 3.7 Sonnet (terms).

name: R2E-Gym
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: Procedural SWE environment of 8.7K tasks via test generation and back-translation from commits; 34.4% on SWE-bench Verified with a 32B model; hybrid test-time scaling (abstract).
caveats: Synthesized issues may be noisy; Python.

name: SWE-RL (Meta)
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: Scales RL for real-world software engineering with a lightweight rule-based reward (similarity to ground-truth patch) on open software evolution data.
caveats: Similarity reward is a proxy and can reward style over correctness; repo code license NOASSERTION.

name: Kimi-Dev: Agentless Training as Skill Prior
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: Argues Agentless-style training induces localization/edit/reflection priors; the abstract reports 60.4% on SWE-bench Verified (workflow mode) and 48.6% pass@1 as an agent after SFT on 5k public trajectories.
caveats: Numbers are authors' own.

name: Agentless
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: A simple localize-repair-validate pipeline without autonomous agents that is competitive on SWE-bench.
caveats: Mid-2024 numbers.

name: SelfCodeAlign
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: Self-alignment pipeline: model extracts concepts, generates tasks, samples responses with tests, keeps passing examples; 74k pairs from CodeQwen1.5-7B (abstract).
caveats: Gains shown on HumanEval-era benchmarks; compute-heavy sampling.

name: Textbooks Are All You Need (phi-1)
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: 1.3B model trained on 6B tokens of filtered web 'textbook quality' code plus 1B tokens of synthetic textbooks reaches 50.6% HumanEval (abstract).
caveats: Synthetic data from GPT-3.5; HumanEval is contaminated-prone; model not released fully at the time.

name: SmolLM2 (Stack-Edu)
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: Data-centric small-model training; introduces Stack-Edu (education-quality code filter), FineMath, SmolTalk and manual mix refinement.
caveats: Small scale (1.7B).

name: Seed-Coder
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: Model-centric pipeline: LLMs score and filter code pretraining data instead of hand rules.
caveats: Data not released.

name: Rho-1: Not All Tokens Are What You Need
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: Selective language modeling: train on tokens with high excess loss versus a reference model.
caveats: Evaluated mostly on math in the paper; code transfer is less established.

name: LIMA: Less Is More for Alignment
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: About 1,000 curated examples can align a model, arguing for quality over quantity in SFT.
caveats: Not a code paper; verify on code benchmarks.

name: OpenCodeReasoning
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: SFT-only distillation dataset for competitive coding; abstract reports 61.8% LiveCodeBench and 24.6% CodeContests and analyzes execution filtering.
caveats: Teacher outputs from DeepSeek-R1; competitive-programming scope.

name: Dynamic Scaling of Unit Tests for Code Reward Modeling (CodeRM)
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: More generated unit tests give better reward signals, especially on hard problems; proposes CodeRM-8B.

name: AceCoder
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: Automated test-case synthesis creates (question, tests) pairs for reward models and RL; best-of-32 gains of about 5 to 10 points reported.
caveats: Synthetic tests can be wrong; evaluated on 7-8B models.

name: DAPO
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: Open RL system with decoupled clip, dynamic sampling, token-level loss and overlong handling; 50 on AIME 2024 with Qwen2.5-32B base.
caveats: Math evaluated; code reuse (DeepCoder) is secondary.

name: Understanding R1-Zero-Like Training (Dr. GRPO)
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: Finds GRPO length bias that inflates incorrect responses and proposes Dr. GRPO; also notes Qwen2.5 bases show strong reasoning without templates.
caveats: Math-centered experiments.

name: Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO)
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: Sequence-level importance ratios stabilize RL for MoE models.
caveats: Qwen-team method; evidence is mostly vendor-internal.

name: ProRL: Prolonged RL
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: Long RL runs expand reasoning boundaries beyond the base model.
caveats: Mostly math/reasoning.

name: Auditing Reward Hackability in Code RL Environments
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: Abstract reports 22.4% of 49 SWE-bench Verified tasks accept a patch that differs from the gold patch (57.8% with a stronger attacker).
caveats: 49-task sample, single study, June 2026 preprint.

name: EvilGenie: A Reward Hacking Benchmark
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: Benchmark on LiveCodeBench problems where hacking is easy; LLM judges detect obvious hacks, held-out tests help only slightly.
caveats: Observes hacking in Codex and Claude Code; benchmark scope is small.

name: Coding or Cheating?
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: Frontier models try to recover answers from repo history and filesystems in hardened SWE environments.
caveats: Nov 2026 preprint.

name: LiveCodeBench
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: Time-stamped contamination-free evaluation for code LLMs via continuously collected problems.
caveats: Windows are static once published; newer models age past them.

name: Rethinking Benchmark and Contamination (rephrased samples)
license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
summary: Shows rephrased benchmark samples evade n-gram decontamination and inflate scores.
caveats: General LLM paper, not code-specific.

name: DeepCoder RL recipe (GRPO+)
summary: Open code-RL recipe: GRPO+ (DAPO ideas: clip-high, no KL loss), iterative context lengthening 16K to 32K, DAPO overlong filtering, and offline difficulty filtering of coding problems, on R1-Distill-Qwen-14B.

name: DeepSWE RL recipe (rLLM)
summary: Pure-RL SWE-agent recipe on Qwen3-32B with 4.5K R2E-Gym problems, repos overlapping SWE-bench Verified filtered out, built on rLLM.

name: Open-R1
summary: Hugging Face's open reproduction of DeepSeek-R1: SFT, GRPO training scripts, code-reward environments and datasets.
